title: 17.2 A 28nm 4.05µJ/Encryption 8.72kHMul/s Reconfigurable Multi-Scheme Fully Homomorphic Encryption Processor for Encrypted Client-Server Computing
problem: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving machine learning but incurs prohibitive power consumption and fabrication costs for bootstrapping operations; supporting multiple FHE schemes (BGV, BFV, CKKS) and diverse client/server primitives while managing intensive memory bottlenecks remains challenging.
motivation: Privacy-preserving ML for collaborative computation demands practical FHE hardware; leveled FHE with designated multiplication depth is more practical than full FHE but requires hardware support for multiple schemes and efficient data movement.
method: The 28nm FHE processor implements reconfigurable architecture supporting BGV, BFV, and CKKS schemes with optimized primitives for both client and server computation patterns; architecture-circuit co-optimizations address (I)NTT and polynomial automorphism overhead while managing on-chip data movement.
key_novelty: First silicon-proven reconfigurable multi-scheme FHE processor supporting both client-side and server-side encrypted computation patterns with integrated memory optimization.
contributions: 28nm reconfigurable multi-scheme FHE processor (BGV, BFV, CKKS)
First silicon-proven solution for both client and server computing patterns
primary_theme: Reconfigurable FHE processor for privacy-preserving ML
